comparator.name: Human Geography and Planning
comparator.academicYear: Current published UvA bachelor curriculum, checked 2026-09-27
comparator.sourceNotes: The official programme is 180 EC over three years. Year 1 is a fixed 60-EC foundation in human geography, spatial planning, urban dynamics, academic skills, GIS, quantitative methods and a regional project. For year 2, the generic target requires one of three 18-EC specialisations; Planning is selected by the neutral official-order tie-break, with coherent planning electives instantiated from the official restricted-choice lists. Year 2 also includes 24 EC of methods and field projects. Year 3 contains a 12-EC thematic elective, 6 EC of thesis methods, 30 EC genuine free choice and a 12-EC bachelor thesis. The English and bilingual routes have the same curriculum.

routeSelection.basis: The normalized target names no specialisation. The official curriculum lists Planning, Human Geography, and Global Urbanism and Transnational Planning as equally substantial 18-EC year-2 specialisations and does not identify one as general. Planning appears first, so it is selected neutrally and independently of UCR fit.

alternatives.label: Cities, people & spatial sustainability
alternatives.concept: Combines social-science analysis of people, institutions, inequality and urban change with environmental systems, spatial data, earth observation, economics and applied sustainability research to understand and improve places.
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum joins urban and social analysis to spatial-environmental methods and sustainability; the label does not imply that UCR offers a dedicated professional planning degree.
progression: Social-science, sustainability, data and research foundations precede advanced urban inequality, environmental governance, earth observation, econometrics and applied research. All prerequisites and planned offerings pass; eight 300-level courses are included.

alternatives.label: Urban governance, inequality & policy
alternatives.concept: Organises sociology, politics, law, economics, psychology and communication around urban inequality, housing, institutions, public decision-making, social movements and the governance of sustainable and inclusive cities.
alternatives.labelReason: The completed programme centres the institutional, distributive and political choices through which cities are governed, while retaining social-research methods and environmental policy.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the closest programme, this route replaces much of the earth-system, spatial-data and environmental-technology sequence with law, political institutions, international relations, diversity, communication, design and public decision-making. Ten courses differ, comfortably exceeding the 30-EC floor.
progression: Sociology, politics, law and research-method foundations precede comparative institutions, urban inequality, rights, governance, communication and advanced policy-facing study. All prerequisites and planned offerings pass; eight 300-level courses are included.

alternatives.label: Globalisation, migration & transnational places
alternatives.concept: Studies how empire, globalisation, migration, political institutions, inequality, race, heritage and social movements shape identities and places across borders, supported by qualitative, quantitative and historical research.
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum visibly shifts the spatial question to global connections, migration, empire, race, heritage and transnational politics without claiming a dedicated geography sequence.
alternatives.distinctness: This route replaces most planning, design, environmental engineering and domestic urban-governance content with empire, international relations, global political economy, migration-related inequality, race, heritage and transnational cultural histories. It differs by at least nine courses from each earlier alternative.
progression: Sociology, politics, history and research foundations precede global political economy, international law, race, heritage, social movements and advanced transnational analysis. All prerequisites and planned offerings pass; eight 300-level courses are included.

selection.assessment: The closest programme integrates the target’s social-spatial, environmental and mixed-method core. The Human Geography and Global Urbanism directions are separately evidenced by official specialisations and produce materially different governance/inequality and transnational-place curricula. All three are mechanically feasible and pairwise differ by at least nine courses, so production stops at the three-alternative maximum.

notes.text: UvA provides a continuous disciplinary sequence in human geography and spatial planning, including dedicated GIS, field projects, planning theory, a named specialisation and a bachelor thesis. UCR can combine strong sociology, politics, economics, sustainability, environmental science, data and research courses, but the fixed Fall 2026 catalogue does not offer the same full geography-and-planning sequence. The UCR alternatives therefore cover related subjects and methods without claiming professional planning equivalence.
